title: Glitch Theory: Art and Semiotics

description.main: Michael Betancourt's study of the glitch as a critical model, tracing it from early abstraction to AI-generated art. Published by Im Pressd in 2023, 192 pages with full-colour illustrations.
description.extended:
A theory of the glitch that reads digital failure as evidence of how images are made and interpreted.

Betancourt argues that a glitch exposes the normally invisible processes behind our interpretations. It arises, he says, from instabilities between human interpretation and autonomous machine operation. The book follows glitches through historical and contemporary media, from early abstraction to AI-generated art. It offers the glitch as a critical model for artists, academics and cultural activists working with contemporary art and tactical media. The volume has 192 pages, all illustrated in colour. Im Pressd published it in November 2023.

Betancourt is an artist and theorist who has worked with databending images and video since the 1990s. His earlier books include Glitch Art in Theory and Practice (Routledge, 2016) and Beyond Spatial Montage: Windowing.
